issues: FollowersView (Connections.js L403-491) does NOT render the amber 'Numeric baseline only' info banner or the yellow-orange 'No historical baseline' warning banner. FollowingView does (L293-313). This is a UX inconsistency: on the Followers tab with count-baseline-only data, users see the net_change (+1280) with no explanation why the itemized names aren't shown, and on the Followers tab with no baseline at all they get no warning banner. Recommend porting the same two banner blocks from FollowingView (L293-313) into FollowersView after the stat-cards grid.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py _snapshot_connections L211-311: correctly separates profile_count (real IG count from fetch_profile, uses cache) from sample_count (len of Apify scraped list, capped at ~200). This is the correct fix for BUG 1.

server.py L246-262: the count-baseline lookup on follower_snapshots is scoped by since_days cutoff AND falls back to most-recent when since_days=0. net_change = real_total - baseline_count works even when no full-list snapshot from that period exists (BUG 2 fix). Good.
server.py L282-289: `if current_usernames:` guard prevents inserting empty connection_snapshots — good hygiene retained.

Connections.js FollowersView L403-491 is missing the two contextual banners present in FollowingView L293-313 (amber 'Numeric baseline only' + yellow-orange 'No historical baseline'). This is not a correctness issue but a UX inconsistency between tabs. Extract the banner block into a reusable <BaselineBanner> component and use in both views.

Connections.js L256-257: `netAdded = netChange != null && netChange > 0 ? netChange : (hasBaseline ? recentlyFollowed.length : null)` — this branches away from named-diff to raw net_change when net_change is positive AND from named-diff (recentlyFollowed) when hasBaseline is true. Slightly confusing branching; when both are available (full-list snapshot AND count snapshot from period), the numeric net_change wins. Acceptable but consider documenting the precedence rule.

Connections.js file is 655 lines — still under the 700 hard threshold from the code-review guidelines, but continuing to grow (was 599 in iteration 5). Recommend splitting into /pages/connections/{FollowingView, FollowersView, CommentsView, StatCard, UserRow, UserCard, QuotaExhausted}.jsx.

Connections.js L270: sublabel condition `sampleCount < profileCount` triggers rendering only when scrape is capped — good. However when profileCount is 0 or null (e.g., failed fetch_profile), the null-safety toLocaleString() call in `value={profileCount?.toLocaleString() ?? '—'}` on L265/L421 works, but the sublabel condition `sampleCount < profileCount` would evaluate `X < undefined` → false, so no sublabel — behavior is safe but could be more explicit.

rca of the issue: BUG 1 root cause: prior _snapshot_connections returned total_count=len(scraped_list) which was hard-capped at ~200 by the Apify actor scraping_solutions~instagram-scraper-followers-following-no-cookies. Fix: added fetch_profile() call inside _snapshot_connections to get real IG follower/following count from the profile-scraper actor, separated into profile_count (real) and sample_count (scraped-list length). Frontend now displays profile_count as the primary value and shows sample_count in a sublabel 'Showing X of Y'. BUG 2 root cause: prior implementation only computed added/removed by full-list set-diff on connection_snapshots. When a full-list baseline from ≥7 days ago didn't exist (which is common — connection_snapshots are inserted only when user opens the Connections page or the daily scheduler runs, and both had gaps), the UI defaulted to '+0/-0' rather than showing net-change from the more frequent follower_snapshots collection (populated every 6h by the scheduler). Fix: query follower_snapshots for a baseline document ≤(now - since_days) regardless of connection_snapshots status, compute net_change = current_profile.count - baseline.count, return has_count_baseline + baseline_count + net_change alongside the full-list added/removed. Frontend now derives netAdded/netLost from net_change first (numeric-only) with the full-list diff as an enrichment when available; renders the amber 'Numeric baseline only' banner to explain to the user why named accounts aren't shown when only a numeric baseline exists.
